title: Joseph and the Izbicer's Hidden Will
hook: the Izbicer taught that God's will can hide inside human choices
carry: god's will can hide inside our choices

segments.voice: Yesterday, the Kotzker rebbe and his demand for truth with no comfort added. Your line: truth, fiercely. Today, a voice that came out of that same fierce room.

Joseph's brothers stand in front of him in Egypt, terrified. Years before, they threw him in a pit and sold him. Now he rules the country's grain, and they need bread. He could punish them. Instead he says something strange: "So now it was not you that sent me hither, but God." They did it, and they remember doing it. And Joseph tells them a second story was running underneath theirs the whole time. One Hasidic teacher pressed that idea into places that still unsettle his readers.
screen: `THE BROTHERS IN EGYPT.` → `IT WAS NOT YOU, BUT GOD.` → `A STORY UNDER THE STORY.`

segments.voice: Hidden will. The teacher is Rabbi Mordechai Yosef Leiner, called the Izbicer after his town, Izbica. Tradition says he learned in the Kotzker's circle before going his own way. His teachings were gathered in a book called Mei HaShiloach, the waters of Shiloah. First, the old line. The Talmud says everything is in the hands of Heaven except the fear of Heaven. Standing in awe of God is your own choice. Second, the Izbicer's push. In his readings, even our choices can carry God's will inside them, hidden. A person acts, sure they're acting alone, and later it turns out something larger was moving through the act. Joseph saw it: "ye thought evil against me; but God meant it unto good." Third, the hard part. The Izbicer reads some uncomfortable stories this way, people in the Torah who seem to break the rules, and asks whether a deeper will was at work. Readers argue over these passages; some find them daring, some unsettling. Fourth, the guardrail. He did not tell people to drop the commandments and follow their urges. In ordinary life, his readers say, a person walks by the law. The hidden will is something you might glimpse, if at all, looking back. You can't see the whole of your own story from inside it: a wrong turn, a closed door, a person who hurt you. The Izbicer doesn't say the hurt was good. He says the last word on what it meant may not be yours to write yet.
screen: `THE IZBICER AND HIS BOOK.` · `IN THE HANDS OF HEAVEN.` · `GOD'S WILL INSIDE OUR CHOICES.` · `SEEN, IF AT ALL, LOOKING BACK.` · then, large: `HIDDEN WILL.`

segments.voice: Bring to mind one thing in your life you still don't understand, not a crisis, just something that never made sense: a plan that fell apart, a meeting you didn't expect. Hold it gently, without explaining it or calling it good, and on each breath out, loosen your grip on needing the answer today. If you pray, you can hold it there, in the hands of Heaven.
Hidden will. The Izbicer's teaching that God's will can hide inside human choices, seen, if at all, only looking back, while ordinary life still walks by the law. Today's word.
Your line: God's will can hide inside our choices. Some stories can only be read looking back. See you tomorrow.

howItsDone: Students of the Izbicer read Mei HaShiloach slowly, often with a teacher, alongside the weekly Torah portion, and his teachings are discussed in Hasidic and other study circles as a way to think about choice and providence.
